transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I work in a woodshop, and, well... if a saw starts up, or someone just walks past the door, I lose track of what I was doing. Even just thinking about another job we have lined up... it pulls me away. And then, before I know it, the whole day is just gone.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to keep moving, or find it hard to stay seated when you need to?

I guess so. Mostly if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates... or if I'm stuck in a long meeting. I just get... wound up inside. Like I need to get up and move around. I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish... especially since my wrist is healed now, so there's no real excuse, but... yeah. It's hard to stay in the chair.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy lately?
No... not really. I mean, I still like building things. Just... having trouble getting them done. But I don't feel hopeless. Just... frustrated, I guess.
Do you often find yourself losing tools, forgetting where you put things, or having trouble keeping track of items you need for your work?

Yeah... all the time. It's... it's a problem. I'm always looking for my tape measure, or my keys. My phone. Even just... the order sheets or notes I was just holding. I set them down and they're gone. It wastes a lot of time. The other guys at the shop... they've started checking up behind me to make sure I have what I need.
Looking back, were you already having trouble focusing or keeping still when you were a kid, or did these issues start more recently?

Yeah... it's not new. Even back in grade school... I guess before I was twelve. 

My teachers were always telling my mother I was bright, but... careless. I was always losing my homework. Or I'd forget the instructions and just... stare out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. So... yeah. It's always been like that.
